claims.text: The economic problem is that resources are finite while wants are unlimited, so choices must be made about how resources are used.

claims.text: The economic problem applies to consumers, workers, producers and governments alike, because each has finite resources facing unlimited wants and each must therefore choose between competing uses.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: An economic good is scarce relative to wants, so obtaining it requires a sacrifice and normally commands a price.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A free good is not scarce: at a zero price, supply exceeds wants, so obtaining it involves no sacrifice and commands no price.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: The test that separates an economic good from a free good is whether a price has to be paid, because a price is the mark of scarcity.
